The ordinance text on American Legal Publishing could not be opened (403), so 'no local technical amendment' rests on ORC 3781.01 (state pack), which lets a city add only rules that don't conflict with the state code, and was not confirmed in Chapter 3111 itself.

fixtures.basis: No Cleveland amendment to the toilet-count table was found on the city's permit, resources, FAQ or ordinances pages, which point to the Ohio Building Code. State law (ORC 3781.01, state pack) allows a municipality only regulations 'not in conflict' with the Board of Building Standards' rules. Cleveland Codified Ordinances Chapters 3111 (Ohio Building Code) and 3133 (Plumbing) could not be opened, so this is 'none found', not 'none exists'. The state pack's counts stand.

permit.exempt_list_quote: Permits are required for all new construction, additions, alterations, changes in use and occupancy, movement, enlargement, replacement, repair, equipment, location, removal, and demolition of every building or structure or any appurtenances connected to such buildings or structures. [...] See the latest edition of the Cleveland Building Code, the Cleveland Zoning Code, the Ohio Building Code and Related Codes [...] for details and exceptions. [...] Minor repairs. Minor repairs to structures may be made without application or notice to the Building Department. Such minor repairs shall not include the cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress, or rearrangement of parts of a structure affecting the egress requirements; nor shall ordinary repairs include addition to, alteration of, replacement or relocation of any standpipe, water supply, sewer, drainage, drain leader, gas, soil, waste, vent or similar piping, electrical wiring or mechanical or other work affecting public health or general safety. Minor repairs can include patching walls and leaking roof coverings, pointing masonry, replacement of shingles, siding and floorboards, where the patching, pointing or replacement is of same material and the scope of replacement is limited to 10% of the wall, floor, ceiling, roof or other building component. Replacement of broken glass or glazing is minor repair, the replacement of window units is an alteration requiring a permit.
permit.note: The quote is the city's one-page 'Permit Requirements' sheet (Division of Construction Permitting, undated PDF). Toilet partitions or compartments are not named there or on the Permits web page; 'partition' in the minor-repairs paragraph means a wall. The Permits page lists 'Replacement: removing an existing building component or system and installing a new one in its place. Example: Replacing a roof, windows or furnace' among projects that require permits, and lists as 'Minor Repairs that DO NOT need a Building Permit' only patching, pointing, same-material replacement up to 10% and broken glass. Ohio's own exempt list (OBC 102.10, quoted in the Columbus pack) doesn't name partitions either. Cleveland Codified Ordinances 3105.01 'Permits Required; Exceptions' could not be opened.
permit.second_quote: Projects That Require Permits [...] Alterations: Reconfiguring interior spaces (e.g., removing or adding non-load-bearing walls) [...] Replacement: removing an existing building component or system and installing a new one in its place. Example: Replacing a roof, windows or furnace. [...] Minor Repairs that DO NOT need a Building Permit: Surface & Structural Finishes: Patching walls; Patching leaking roof coverings; Pointing masonry; Replacing shingles (same material, ≤10% of roof area); Replacing siding (same material, ≤10% of wall area); Replacing floorboards (same material, ≤10% of floor area). Glass & Glazing: Replacing broken glass or glazing (not full window units)
permit.state_quote: 102.10 Work exempt from approval. Approval is not required for the following work [...] 6. Finishes not regulated by this code, decorating, or other work defined as maintenance or minor repair.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Cleveland job sites. Price your restroom, choose a material and see the Ohio rules Cleveland enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Cleveland hospitals, schools, offices and manufacturing plants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Ohio's statewide building rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and Cleveland enforces them. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Cleveland requires a permit for alterations, replacements and repairs to a building. Minor repairs need none: the city's examples are patching walls and replacing up to 10% of a floor, wall or roof covering with the same material. Neither list names toilet partitions. Ask the Cleveland Department of Building and Housing whether your replacement needs a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the Cleveland Department of Building and Housing
page.install_rule: Cleveland requires contractors to be registered with the city, bonded and insured, through the Department of Building and Housing before pulling building permits. Ohio licenses only five commercial trades at state level: electrical, HVAC, hydronics, plumbing and refrigeration. Partition installation isn't one of them. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who pulls a permit in Cleveland must be registered with the city first.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, county and city projects over $250,000 for new construction or $75,000 for remodeling, Ohio law requires at least the wage the state sets for each trade in each county; school district projects are exempt from that law. The state publishes its Cuyahoga County rates on a portal that needs a login. On federally funded building work in Cuyahoga County, the federal rate for a carpenter is $37.52 an hour plus $23.50 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8% in Cleveland: 5.75% state, 1.25% Cuyahoga County and 1% transit authority.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals and medical buildings:** phenolic or stainless steel that stands up to frequent disinfecting, with full-height privacy stalls in public and staff restrooms.
